Norah's Kitchen

Restaurant reservation chatbot · A made-up restaurant with a real, working booking system

Free to run · Always online

A guest opens the restaurant website, taps Reserve a Table, and chats in the middle of the page. The chatbot asks for a name, date, time, number of guests and phone number — one at a time if anything is missing. It then books, changes, cancels or looks up the reservation and replies with a booking number like NK-1007. Every booking is saved for real in a simple spreadsheet, so it can always be checked.

Book a table

Makes sure the date hasn't already passed, holds the table for 15 minutes, and gives the guest a booking number.

Change a booking

Changes the original booking — for example, 7pm to 8pm — instead of making a second, duplicate booking.

Cancel & look up

Cancels a booking but keeps a record of it. Guests can also look up their booking details and re-book if they change their mind.

Answer questions

Answers questions about hours, location and parking — 123 Main Ave, open daily 11:00 AM–10:00 PM. Groups of more than 8 are asked to call 123-456-7890.

How it works — In simple steps

How it works, step by step

What happens when a guest sends one message. The guest just sees a friendly chat. Behind the scenes, a few services work together to understand the message, check the bookings, and send a reply.

Follow the arrows to see where the message goes next.

Step 1 · Guest

Guest on their phone

Opens the site and types in plain language — “book for 4 tomorrow at 7” is enough.

→
Step 2 · Website

The chat box on the website

The website is hosted for free on GitHub Pages. The guest types there, and their message is sent on.

→
Step 3 · Behind the scenes

Cloudflare

This keeps everything running online. It remembers the conversation, knows today's date, and makes sure the booking rules are followed.

→
Step 4 · The AI

Google Gemini

The AI that understands what the guest is asking. It can answer a simple question right away, or check and update the bookings when needed.

If a booking needs to be checked or changed ↓

What the chatbot can do with a booking

It chooses the right action on its own
Check bookingsLooks at the saved bookings first — to see what's available and to find a guest's booking.Look up
Add a bookingSaves a new booking and gives it the next booking number, like NK-1008.Add
Change a bookingUpdates the same booking — the date, time, number of guests, name or phone number.Change
Cancel a bookingMarks the booking as cancelled. A record is kept, so it can be found again later.Cancel
All bookings are saved here ↓
Step 5 · Where bookings are saved

Google Sheets — “Bookings”

A simple spreadsheet that holds every booking: booking number, name, date, time, number of guests, phone number, and whether it's confirmed or cancelled. Easy for anyone to open and read.

↔
Memory

Remembers the conversation

The chatbot remembers what was already said in the same visit — like the guest's name and booking number — so they don't have to repeat themselves.

Then the reply comes back: once the booking is checked or saved, the guest sees a clear confirmation in the chat with their booking number. If a lot of people message at the exact same moment, it may take a few seconds longer — it tries again on its own, so the guest doesn't see an error.
What I used to build it

GitHub Pages

Where the restaurant website lives online. Free, and live at the link above.

Cloudflare

Keeps the chatbot running online all the time. Free, and no card was needed to set it up.

Google Gemini

The AI behind the chat. It understands what guests write and replies in a natural, friendly way.

Google Sheets

Where all the bookings are saved — a simple spreadsheet that anyone can open and read.

Google

Connects the chatbot safely to that booking spreadsheet, and only to that spreadsheet.

The design

A simple, elegant look for the website and chat, made to be clear and easy to use on a phone.
